strategies.name: support_bounce_scalp_to_resistance
strategies.entry_summary: After the first 5 to 15 minutes, identify a support level on the 5-minute chart, especially where price bounces from the 13 EMA or later the 200 EMA, and enter when price comes down into that support and holds/bounces.
strategies.exit_summary: Take profit quickly into the next resistance / after the ensuing pop; the speaker repeatedly frames the trade as getting in at support and selling at resistance without overstaying.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for the opening 5 to 15 minutes to establish support, then buy the touch/bounce of the 13 EMA acting as support
variants.target_note: exit on the quick move up / at resistance
variants.transcript_quote: the stock came down and it hit right there that's our entry for a scalp okay and then from here we got in in and then look at one green candle two gr

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: re-enter on another touch of the same support level
variants.target_note: exit after the bounce forms / at resistance
variants.transcript_quote: it came back down again boom same level you enter here and then boom you got this move now we have formed this is your exit

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: after 13 EMA support fails, use the 200 EMA / deeper support as the buy zone
variants.target_note: ride it to resistance and exit
variants.transcript_quote: you get in here as support and you ride it to resistance and you exit okay another quick Scout this one off a deeper support sitting at the 200 EMA

result.enumeration_note: The transcript clearly teaches one runnable long support-bounce scalp skeleton with variants at 13 EMA and 200 EMA support; the later downside 'big move' mention has an entry direction but only a gestural hindsight exit ('you want to exit right there'), so it is not promoted to a separate strategy under Rule 1.
